parts.problem_md:
The graph below can be used to change between Australian dollars and euros

![Graph showing a linear relationship between Australian dollars, on the x-axis, and euros, on the y-axis, ranging from 0 to 70 and 0 to 50 respectively.](assets/001-graph-showing-a-linear-relationship-between-aust.png)

Use the graph to change

(i) 35 Australian dollars to euros

(ii) 20 euros to Australian dollars
parts.solution_md:
(i)

> *Use your ruler to draw a line up from 35 on the x axis until it meets the line*

![A conversion graph showing Australian dollars on the x axis and euros on the y axis](assets/002-a-conversion-graph-showing-australian-dollars-on.png)

**Final answer:** **22**

**[B1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Your answer should be in the range 21.5 to 22.5.

(ii)

> *Use your ruler to draw a line across from 20 euros on the y axis until it meets the line*

![A conversion graph showing Australian dollars on the x axis and euros on the y axis](assets/003-a-conversion-graph-showing-australian-dollars-on.png)

**Final answer:** **32**

**[B1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Your answer should be in the range 31 to 32.

parts.problem_md:
Lachlan changes 500 Australian dollars to euros.

Work out how many euros he should receive.
parts.solution_md:
> *The graph does not go up to 500 Australian dollars, so choose a factor of 500 that is on the graph and then scale up*

![A conversion graph with Australian dollars on the x axis and euros on the y axis](assets/004-a-conversion-graph-with-australian-dollars-on-th.png)

$50\mathrm{Australian} \mathrm{dollars}=31.5\mathrm{euros}$

**[M1]**

> *Multiply both sides by 10*

$500\mathrm{Australian} \mathrm{dollars}=315\mathrm{euros}$

**Final answer:** **315 euros**

**[A1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Answers between 300-325 are accepted.
